Both partners lead with the right stick, so strikes cross diagonally; nobody mirrors.
Four dandiya staples measure 90 to 126 BPM on SongBPM; at 126 BPM one 4-clap cycle lasts 3.8 seconds.

faqs.question: How do I hold dandiya sticks so I don't hit my fingers?
faqs.answer: Hold each stick in its lower third with your thumb along the side, and strike only with the top third. With 18-inch sticks, stand roughly 75 to 90 cm from your partner so the tips meet at chest height instead of over your hands.

faqs.question: Do both partners start with the right stick?
faqs.answer: Yes. In both the 2-clap and the 4-clap, your right stick meets your partner's right stick, so the strike crosses diagonally between you. Nobody mirrors. If one of you is left-handed, agree on the right-first order before the song starts.

faqs.question: How many times do you hit your partner's sticks in one round?
faqs.answer: Two times in the 2-clap, which runs over four counts, and four times in the 4-clap, which runs over eight. The other counts are taps on your own sticks, plus a no-strike count 8 in the 4-clap when the lines shift.

faqs.question: What should I do if I lose the count halfway through a song?
faqs.answer: Do not stop, because the line keeps rotating around you. Skip to the next tap on your own sticks, which falls on count 1, 4 or 7 of the 4-clap, and pick the pattern up from there.

faqs.question: Can I dance dandiya with the same partner all night?
faqs.answer: Only if the two of you play as a fixed pair. In the usual two-line format, everyone moves on at count 8, so at 126 BPM you face someone new roughly every 3.8 seconds. Some venues move on two places at a time.

faqs.question: What length should dandiya sticks be?
faqs.answer: A 2014 PTI report on Godhra's dandiya makers describes sticks of about 18 inches, made from mango or baval wood and decorated with lace, beads and ghungroos. Your standing distance from your partner is set by that length.

faqs.question: Is dandiya harder than garba for a beginner?
faqs.answer: It asks for more coordination because you have to time strikes against another person, not only follow a circle. The 2-clap at about 90 BPM is a gentle start, and most people can learn it standing still before they add footwork.

faqs.question: How many calories does an hour of dandiya burn?
faqs.answer: The 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities rates folk dancing at 5.0 MET when moderate and 9.8 MET when vigorous. For a 60 kg dancer that is roughly 300 to 588 kcal an hour, depending on the pace of the set.

faqs.question: Which songs are good for practising dandiya at home?
faqs.answer: Pick one slow and one fast song. SongBPM lists Maine Payal Hai Chhankai at 90 BPM, Nagada Sang Dhol at 113 BPM, Shubhaarambh at 115 BPM and Chogada at 126 BPM double-time. These are algorithmic estimates, so treat them as approximate.

faqs.question: How do I ask one person to be my dandiya partner?
faqs.answer: Ask them directly, or send an interactive invitation such as SubhSandesh's Be My Dandiya Partner page, which ends in a downloadable Dandiya Pass when they say yes. It is a one-to-one invite in English and does not find you a partner.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Dandiya Partner Steps: The 2-Clap and 4-Clap Patterns, Counted

Dandiya partner steps come down to two patterns. In the 2-clap, you tap your own sticks, then strike your partner's right stick, tap your own again, then strike their left, over four counts. The 4-clap stretches that to an eight-count with four partner strikes, and on count 8 both lines shift so everyone faces someone new.

This page is built to be read on a phone at the venue, because that is where most people will open it: 48.3% of views of pages shared through SubhSandesh happen on a phone (27,725 of 57,456). Festival prep also runs late. In the one festival we have measured, Raksha Bandhan 2026, 49.4% of pages were built on the festival day itself (n=89, a different festival used as the nearest analogue). Below are both patterns as count tables, the rotation, song tempos in BPM, the mistakes that snag two dancers, and how hard the dancing is on your body.

## What are dandiya partner steps?

Dandiya partner steps are the fixed stick patterns two dancers play facing each other in dandiya raas, the paired stick dance of Navratri. Each person holds two sticks, and every pattern alternates strikes on your own sticks with strikes on your partner's.

The rhythm underneath is usually Kaherva, an eight-beat cycle. The sticks are short: a 2014 PTI report on [Godhra's dandiya makers](https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/godhra-muslims-earn-living-by-crafting-dandiyas-for-navratri-114092500566_1.html) describes them as about 18 inches long, carved from mango or baval wood and decorated with lace, beads and ghungroos. That length decides how far apart you stand.

## Stance and stick grip before count 1

Stand facing your partner about one stick-length plus a forearm apart, roughly 75 to 90 cm with 18-inch sticks. Closer than that and your strikes land on hands; further and you lean, which kills your balance on the turn.

Hold each stick in its lower third, thumb along the side, not wrapped over the end. Strike with the top third only. Keep elbows bent at about 90 degrees, so the stick tip meets your partner's at chest height.

Keep knees soft, with one small bounce per count.

## The 2-clap pattern, written as counts

The 2-clap is the beginner pattern: four counts, two strikes with your partner. Learn it standing still before you add any footwork.

| Count | Your sticks | Partner contact | Feet |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tap your own two sticks together at chest height | None | Step right, small |
| 2 | Your right stick strikes their right stick | 1st strike | Close left to right |
| 3 | Tap your own sticks together again | None | Step left, small |
| 4 | Your left stick strikes their left stick | 2nd strike | Close right to left |

Your right meets their right, so the strike crosses diagonally between you. Both partners do the identical pattern at the same moment; nobody mirrors. Say "own, right, own, left" aloud for the first 16 cycles.

## The 4-clap pattern on an eight-count

The 4-clap is the pattern most organised dandiya nights settle into: eight counts, four strikes with your partner, and a quarter-turn away in the middle. It matches the eight beats of Kaherva, so each cycle fills one full rhythmic cycle of the song.

| Count | Your sticks | Partner contact | Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tap your own sticks | None | Face partner |
| 2 | Right stick to their right | 1st strike | Face partner |
| 3 | Left stick to their left | 2nd strike | Face partner |
| 4 | Tap your own sticks | None | Quarter-turn to your left, away from them |
| 5 | Right stick to their right | 3rd strike | Turn back to face them |
| 6 | Left stick to their left | 4th strike | Face partner |
| 7 | Tap your own sticks | None | Begin moving |
| 8 | Sticks up, no strike | None | Step forward past right shoulders to the next partner |

Count 4 is where beginners drift. Turn only a quarter at first; the full spin comes once you can land count 5 without looking down.

## How the partner rotation moves down the line

Dandiya nights usually form two parallel lines with partners facing. On count 8, both lines step forward and pass right shoulder to right shoulder, so each person meets the next dancer in the opposite line.

Some venues move on two places instead of one; watch the first two cycles before you join. At the end of a line, you turn and join the opposite line, so the movement never stops.

A 4:10 song at 126 beats per minute holds about 65 eight-count cycles. If the line rotates every cycle, you play with a new partner every 3.8 seconds, which is why "dandiya with partner" rarely means one partner all night unless the two of you dance a pair inside the line.

## How fast are slow and fast dandiya sets?

The four dandiya staples we checked sit between 90 and 126 BPM. SongBPM, a tempo database built from streaming metadata, lists [Nagada Sang Dhol at 113 BPM](https://songbpm.com/@shreya-ghoshal/nagada-sang-dhol), Shubhaarambh at 115 BPM and Maine Payal Hai Chhankai at 90 BPM. It gives [Chogada as 63 BPM, "double-time at 126 BPM"](https://songbpm.com/@darshan-raval/chogada); dancers step to the 126.

These are algorithmic estimates, and live dhol players speed up through a set, but they turn "slow" and "fast" into numbers.

| Pattern and tempo | Counts per cycle | Partner strikes per cycle | Seconds per cycle | Approximate effort band (2024 Compendium) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2-clap at 90 BPM (slow set) | 4 | 2 | 2.7 | Folk, moderate: 5.0 MET |
| 4-clap at 113–115 BPM | 8 | 4 | 4.2 | Between 5.0 and 9.8 MET |
| 4-clap at 126 BPM (fast set) | 8 | 4 | 3.8 | Folk, vigorous: 9.8 MET |
| Half-time 4-clap at 126 BPM | 16 beats | 4 | 7.6 | Closer to 5.0 MET |

Learn at 90, move to the 4-clap around 113, and only spin at 126 once count 5 lands every time. When a fast set outruns you, strike on every other beat: the half-time row keeps you in the pattern at half the strike rate.

On effort, the [2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities](https://pacompendium.com/dancing) rates folk dancing at 5.0 MET when moderate and 9.8 MET when vigorous. For a 60 kg dancer that works out to roughly 300 and 588 kcal an hour. Drink water between sets, wear flat shoes, and step out if you feel dizzy.

## Five mistakes that snag two dancers

Each of these is a timing or spacing problem, not a talent problem.

### 1. Hitting knuckles

Knuckles get hit when the strike lands on the bottom half of the stick. Hold low, strike high, and keep the 75 to 90 cm gap. We found no clinical study of dandiya hand injuries, so treat this as practice advice rather than a measured risk.

### 2. Mirroring your partner

Mirror-work snags when one partner leads with the left on count 2. Both play right on count 2, left on count 3, so the strike crosses. If your partner is left-handed, agree on the right-first order before the song starts.

### 3. Watching your own hands

Looking down breaks the coupling with your partner. A [2012 PLOS ONE study by Romero and colleagues](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0044761) found people's rhythmic arm movements spontaneously fell into time with a moving target, and more strongly when they visually tracked it. Watch your partner's right stick tip, not your own.

### 4. Swinging hard to sound good

A hard swing slows your return, so you miss count 3. Strike from the wrist with about 10 cm of travel; the sound comes from wood, not force.

### 5. Freezing after a missed count

Stopping dead jams the line, because the people behind you still rotate on count 8. Skip to the next own-stick tap (count 1, 4 or 7) and rejoin.

## Why rapport with your partner helps the timing

Pairs who feel at ease with each other move more in time. In a [2025 PLOS ONE study by Scheer and colleagues](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0333709), 34 pairs of strangers did a jigsaw either together or apart, then jumped on facing trampolines. Pairs who had cooperated moved more in sync, and the rapport they felt at the start mattered even more.

That is a lab finding about trampolines, not dandiya, so treat it as a hint: practise the 2-clap together before the line forms.

If there is one specific person you want across from you, [Be My Dandiya Partner](https://subhsandesh.in/dandiya-partner) is an interactive invitation for exactly that ask. They clash a pair of dandiya sticks to open it, light nine diyas that each show one of your lines, play a short dhol-beat game and pick the colour they will twirl in. Its eight preset songs include Chogada, Nagada Sang Dhol and Shubhaarambh, the same three tempos in the table above. A yes ends in a 1080×1920 Dandiya Pass sized for an Instagram Story, and you can set an optional password; 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect their page before sharing it (2,000 of 5,199).

Be clear on its limits. It is a one-to-one invitation for your love, your crush or a best friend as a garba buddy, not a group or society invite, and its page is in English. It does not find you a partner. If the plan is a whole evening rather than a dance, [an invitation with a countdown to a planned day](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) suits that better.

## When this page is the wrong tool

Counts cannot show footwork style, the spin on count 4, or the regional variants some venues teach. For those, a class or a slowed-down video beats any table; Sharad Navratri runs 11–19 October 2026 and 30 September–8 October 2027.

Use this page for what video does badly: strike order, the turn count and practice tempo.

## Sources

- Press Trust of India via Business Standard, "Godhra Muslims earn living by crafting 'dandiyas' for Navratri", 25 September 2014.
- Romero, Coey, Schmidt and Richardson, "Movement Coordination or Movement Interference", PLOS ONE 7(9): e44761, 17 September 2012.
- Scheer, Bowling, Hungerländer, Fitch and Horn, "Work together, move together", PLOS ONE 20(10): e0333709, 22 October 2025.
- Compendium of Physical Activities, 2024 Adult Compendium, Dancing codes 03031 and 03033, 2024.
- SongBPM, tempo pages for Chogada and Nagada Sang Dhol (no publication date; read 12 October 2026).
